chunks: Muhammad ibn Abi Abdillah from Muawiya ibn Hakim from Abdullah ibn al-Mughira from Abu al-Hasan al-Awwal (peace be upon him)

Regarding a woman who had post-childbirth bleeding (nifas), so she left the prayer for thirty days, then she became clean, then she saw blood after that. He (peace be upon him) said: 'She should leave the prayer, because her days are the days of purity, and the days of post-childbirth bleeding have passed.'
ai.seo_question: What is the ruling for a woman who sees blood after her post-childbirth bleeding period ends?
ai.summary: In this hadith from *Al-Kafi*, Imam al-Sadiq (AS) clarifies that once the maximum thirty-day period of post-childbirth bleeding (nifas) has elapsed, any subsequent blood is treated as menstrual or non-nifas blood, yet the specific ruling here emphasizes that she continues to abstain from prayer based on the completion of her established nifas days. This ruling highlights the Shia jurisprudential principle that the thirty-day mark serves as the definitive upper limit for nifas, distinguishing it from regular menstruation (hayd) which typically has a shorter maximum duration. The context underscores the practical application of 'days of purity' versus 'days of nifas' in determining ritual status after childbirth.
